laws.title: Hands-Free Driving Law
laws.subtitle: GA Code §40-6-241.2 — No handheld devices while driving
laws.fullDescription: Georgia prohibits holding or using handheld electronic devices while driving. Handheld device use while driving is banned.
laws.penalty: $50 first offense, $100 second, $150 third+.
laws.exceptions: Emergency 911 calls are exempt from hands-free requirements.

quiz.q: Is handheld phone use banned while driving in Georgia?
quiz.explanation: Georgia: all handheld device use while driving is banned (Hands-Free Georgia Act, 2018).

laws.title: Non-Resident Hunting & Fishing License
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §27-2-5 — Non-residents must purchase licenses
laws.fullDescription: Non-residents must obtain a valid Georgia hunting or fishing license before taking game or fish. Annual non-resident fishing licenses cost approximately $11; hunting licenses cost approximately $75. Some species require additional tags.
laws.penalty: Class B misdemeanor or felony; fines up to $1000 plus equipment forfeiture.
laws.exceptions: Residents are exempt from non-resident fees.

quiz.q: What is the penalty for hunting without a license in Georgia?
quiz.explanation: Hunting without a license in Georgia is a Class B misdemeanor with fines up to $1000.

laws.title: Impaired Driving (DUI/DWI)
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §40-6-391 — 0.08% BAC limit
laws.fullDescription: Georgia prohibits operating a vehicle with a BAC of 0.08% or higher. Commercial drivers: 0.04%. Drivers under 21: 0.02 BAC. Implied consent laws apply.
laws.penalty: First offense: $300–$1,000 fine, 12-month license suspension, up to 1 year jail. Subsequent offenses carry mandatory minimums and longer suspensions.
laws.exceptions: None — even prescription medication impairment can result in DUI charges.

quiz.q: What BAC triggers a DUI in Georgia for regular drivers?
quiz.explanation: The legal BAC limit in Georgia is 0.08% for regular drivers, consistent with all US states.

laws.title: Open Container Law
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §40-6-253 — No open alcohol in vehicles
laws.fullDescription: Georgia prohibits open alcoholic beverage containers in the passenger area of motor vehicles on public roads. Open container law applies to driver and passengers.
laws.penalty: $200 fine; applies to driver and passengers.
laws.exceptions: Passengers in for-hire vehicles (taxis, limos) may be exempt.

quiz.q: Can passengers drink alcohol in a private car in Georgia?
quiz.explanation: Georgia's open container law applies to all vehicle occupants.

laws.title: Recreational Cannabis — Not Legal
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §16-13-30 — Recreational cannabis NOT legal
laws.fullDescription: Georgia: Recreational cannabis is illegal in Georgia. Possession of any amount is a criminal offense. Medical cannabis (low-THC oil, up to 5% THC) is legal for registered patients.
laws.penalty: Possession under 1 oz: misdemeanor, up to 1 year. Over 1 oz: felony.
laws.exceptions: Medical patients exempt.

quiz.q: Is recreational cannabis legal in Georgia?
quiz.explanation: Recreational cannabis is illegal in Georgia; only low-THC medical cannabis oil is permitted.

laws.title: Medical Cannabis — Legal
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §31-2A-2 — Medical cannabis program
laws.fullDescription: Georgia has a limited medical cannabis program — only low-THC oil (≤5% THC) is permitted for registered patients with qualifying conditions.
laws.penalty: Non-patients face criminal charges.
laws.exceptions: Registered patients are exempt from possession penalties.

quiz.q: Does Georgia have a medical cannabis program?
quiz.explanation: Georgia has a medical cannabis program.

laws.title: Firearm Carry Law — Constitutional
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §16-11-126 — Constitutional state
laws.fullDescription: Georgia is a constitutional state. Georgia passed constitutional carry in 2022 (SB 319) — eligible adults 21+ may carry a concealed handgun without a permit. Permits still offered for reciprocity.
laws.penalty: Carrying while prohibited: felony.
laws.exceptions: Firearms prohibited in schools, courts, and government buildings.

quiz.q: What type of carry law does Georgia have?
quiz.explanation: Georgia has constitutional — permitless carry for eligible adults since 2022

laws.title: Background Check Requirements
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §18 USC 922 — Federal NICS checks at licensed dealers
laws.fullDescription: All firearm purchases from licensed dealers in Georgia require a federal NICS background check. Georgia does not require background checks for private gun sales.
laws.penalty: Straw purchases or sales to prohibited persons: federal felony up to 10 years.
laws.exceptions: Transfers between immediate family members may be exempt.

quiz.q: Does Georgia require background checks for private gun sales?
quiz.explanation: Georgia only requires background checks for licensed dealer gun sales.

laws.title: Stand Your Ground / Castle Doctrine
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §16-3-23.1 — Stand Your Ground
laws.fullDescription: Georgia has a Stand Your Ground law with no duty to retreat anywhere a person has a legal right to be.
laws.penalty: N/A — this law provides a defense against criminal charges.
laws.exceptions: Force not justified if defender is committing a crime or the intruder is a co-resident.

quiz.q: Does Georgia have a Stand Your Ground law?
options: No — duty to retreat outside home
quiz.explanation: Georgia: Stand Your Ground — no duty to retreat anywhere you have a legal right to be.

laws.title: Minimum Wage Law
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §Labor Code — $5.15/hour minimum wage
laws.fullDescription: Georgia's minimum wage is $5.15/hour (2024). Georgia's state minimum wage is only $5.15/hr, but the federal minimum of $7.25/hr applies. Some cities like Atlanta have passed higher local minimums.
laws.penalty: Employers violating minimum wage: back wages, double damages, and attorney fees.
laws.exceptions: Tipped workers may have a lower base wage.

quiz.q: What is the minimum wage in Georgia?
quiz.explanation: Georgia's minimum wage is $5.15/hour.

laws.title: At-Will Employment
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §Labor Code — Employment at will doctrine
laws.fullDescription: Georgia follows at-will employment. Employers may terminate for any legal reason; employees may quit anytime. at-will employment with standard exceptions.
laws.penalty: N/A — at-will is the default standard.
laws.exceptions: Termination for illegal reasons (discrimination, retaliation) is prohibited.

quiz.q: Can an Georgia employer fire an employee without giving a reason?
quiz.explanation: Georgia is an at-will employment state — employers may generally terminate without cause.

laws.title: Right-to-Work Law — Yes
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §Labor Code — Georgia is a right-to-work state
laws.fullDescription: Georgia is a right-to-work state. Georgia is a right-to-work state. Union membership cannot be required as a condition of employment.
laws.penalty: N/A — this governs labor relations framework.
laws.exceptions: Federal employees and some categories are governed by federal law.

quiz.q: Is Georgia a right-to-work state?
quiz.explanation: Georgia is a right-to-work state.

laws.title: Non-Compete Agreement Enforceability
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §Business Code — Non-compete enforceability rules
laws.fullDescription: Georgia: Non-compete agreements enforced if reasonable in scope and duration.
laws.penalty: Overly broad agreements may be voided or reformed by courts.
laws.exceptions: Agreements protecting legitimate trade secrets are most favored.

quiz.q: Are non-compete agreements automatically enforceable in Georgia?
quiz.explanation: Georgia: Courts assess reasonableness of non-competes.

laws.title: Paid Sick Leave — Not Required
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §Labor Code — No statewide mandate
laws.fullDescription: Georgia: Georgia has no statewide paid sick leave mandate. Atlanta passed a local ordinance, but the state has limited local sick leave laws.
laws.penalty: N/A
laws.exceptions: Independent contractors are generally not covered.

quiz.q: Does Georgia require employers to provide paid sick leave?
quiz.explanation: Georgia: Georgia has no statewide paid sick leave requirement.

laws.title: Unemployment Insurance
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §Labor Code — Unemployment benefits
laws.fullDescription: Georgia unemployment insurance provides benefits to eligible workers. Maximum weekly benefit: $365 for up to 14 weeks. Workers must have earned at least $1500 in the base period.
laws.penalty: Filing fraudulent claims: repayment plus penalties and possible criminal charges.
laws.exceptions: Self-employed and independent contractors are generally ineligible for regular UI.

quiz.q: What is the maximum weekly unemployment benefit in Georgia?
quiz.explanation: Georgia's maximum weekly unemployment benefit is $365.

laws.title: Workers' Compensation
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §Labor Code — Mandatory workers' comp coverage
laws.fullDescription: Georgia requires employers with 3 or more employees to carry workers' compensation insurance. Covers medical costs and lost wages for work-related injuries.
laws.penalty: Employers without coverage: fines up to $5000/day, personal liability for claims.
laws.exceptions: Sole proprietors and some domestic workers may be exempt.

quiz.q: How many employees trigger workers' comp requirements in Georgia?
quiz.explanation: Georgia requires workers' comp for employers with 3 or more employees.

laws.title: Independent Contractor Classification
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §Labor Code — Worker classification rules
laws.fullDescription: Georgia uses Common law control test to classify workers. Worker classification uses the common law control test.
laws.penalty: Misclassification: back taxes, penalties, and retroactive benefits liability.
laws.exceptions: Licensed professionals may have different classification standards.

quiz.q: What test does Georgia use for worker classification?
quiz.explanation: Georgia uses the Common law control test for worker classification.

laws.title: Child Labor Laws
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §Labor Code — Restrictions on youth employment
laws.fullDescription: Georgia restricts employment of minors. Children under 14: very limited jobs only. Ages 14–15: restricted hours. Most minors under 18 need work permits. Federal child labor protections apply with state additions.
laws.penalty: Employers violating child labor laws: fines up to $10000 per violation.
laws.exceptions: Family farms and limited entertainment work have exemptions.

quiz.q: At what age do minors generally need work permits in Georgia?
quiz.explanation: Most Georgia minors under 18 need work permits for regular employment.

laws.title: Equal Pay Act
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §Civil Rights Code — Equal pay for equal work
laws.fullDescription: Georgia prohibits pay discrimination based on sex for substantially equal work. Equal pay laws prohibit sex-based wage discrimination.
laws.penalty: Back pay, compensatory damages, and attorney fees for violations.
laws.exceptions: Pay differences justified by seniority, merit, or non-sex factors are permitted.

quiz.q: What agency enforces equal pay laws in Georgia?
quiz.explanation: Georgia's civil rights agency and the federal EEOC both enforce equal pay laws.

laws.title: Anti-Discrimination in Employment
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §Civil Rights Code — Protected classes in Georgia
laws.fullDescription: Georgia prohibits employment discrimination based on race, religion, color, national origin, sex, age (40+), and disability. Standard protected classes under state civil rights law.
laws.penalty: Compensatory damages, back pay, reinstatement, and attorney fees.
laws.exceptions: Religious organizations may have limited exemptions for certain positions.

quiz.q: How many employees must an Georgia employer have before anti-discrimination laws apply?
quiz.explanation: Georgia anti-discrimination laws apply to employers with 15 or more employees.

laws.title: Landlord Entry Notice Requirement
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §Landlord-Tenant Act — 24-hour notice required
laws.fullDescription: Georgia landlords must give tenants 24 hours' written notice before entering for non-emergency purposes. Entry must be at reasonable times.
laws.penalty: Unlawful entry may entitle tenant to damages or lease termination.
laws.exceptions: Emergencies (fire, flood, imminent harm) allow immediate entry without notice.

quiz.q: How many hours notice must Georgia landlords give before entering?
quiz.explanation: Georgia landlords must give 24 hours' notice before non-emergency entry.

laws.title: Security Deposit Rules
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §Landlord-Tenant Act — Two months' rent maximum deposit
laws.fullDescription: Georgia: Maximum security deposit is Two months' rent. Deposits must be returned within 30 days of move-out with an itemized statement of deductions.
laws.penalty: Landlord who wrongfully withholds deposit may owe double damages plus attorney fees.
laws.exceptions: Deposits for pets may be separate in some cases.

quiz.q: How many days does a Georgia landlord have to return a security deposit?
quiz.explanation: Georgia landlords have 30 days to return security deposits after move-out.

laws.title: Rent Control Status — Not Statewide
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §Housing Code — No statewide rent control
laws.fullDescription: Georgia: Georgia state law prohibits local rent control ordinances.
laws.penalty: N/A — this is a policy/regulatory matter.
laws.exceptions: Federally subsidized housing has separate rent rules.

quiz.q: Does Georgia have statewide rent control?
quiz.explanation: Georgia: Georgia prohibits local rent control laws.

laws.title: Eviction Process & Tenant Protections
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §Landlord-Tenant Act — Notice and court process required
laws.fullDescription: Georgia landlords must provide: 5 days notice for nonpayment; 10 days for violations; 30 days for no-cause termination. Court filing required after notice expires.
laws.penalty: Self-help eviction (changing locks, removing belongings) is illegal.
laws.exceptions: Emergency situations may allow expedited proceedings.

quiz.q: How many days notice for non-payment of rent before eviction in Georgia?
quiz.explanation: Georgia requires 5 days notice for nonpayment of rent before filing for eviction.

laws.title: Short-Term Rental (STR) Regulations
laws.subtitle: Local codes — Regulated locally
laws.fullDescription: Georgia: STR regulations vary by municipality.
laws.penalty: Operating without required licenses: fines and possible closure.
laws.exceptions: Owner-occupied properties renting a single room may have reduced requirements.

quiz.q: Are short-term rentals (Airbnb) regulated in Georgia?
quiz.explanation: Georgia regulates STRs primarily at the local level with varying requirements by city.

laws.title: Property Tax
laws.subtitle: Local codes — Average 0.90% effective rate
laws.fullDescription: Georgia: Average effective property tax rate is approximately 0.90%. Georgia has relatively low property taxes. Homestead exemptions significantly reduce taxes for primary residents.
laws.penalty: Delinquent taxes accrue interest and may result in tax lien or foreclosure.
laws.exceptions: Senior citizens and disabled veterans often receive exemptions. Senior and veteran exemptions available.

quiz.q: What is the approximate average effective property tax rate in Georgia?
quiz.explanation: Georgia's average effective property tax rate is approximately 0.90%.

laws.title: Homestead Exemption
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §48-5-44 — $2,000 assessed value reduction homestead exemption
laws.fullDescription: Georgia: Georgia's homestead exemption reduces the assessed value of primary homes by $2,000 for county taxes. Additional exemptions for seniors.
laws.penalty: N/A — this is a protection for homeowners.
laws.exceptions: Does not protect against tax liens, mortgage foreclosures, or mechanic's liens.

quiz.q: What is Georgia's homestead exemption?
quiz.explanation: Georgia's homestead exemption is $2,000 assessed value reduction.

laws.title: State Income Tax — Yes — flat 5.49% (2024)
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §48-7-20 — Yes — flat 5.49% (2024)
laws.fullDescription: Georgia: Georgia is transitioning to a flat income tax rate of 5.49% in 2024, dropping from a tiered system.
laws.penalty: Tax evasion: civil penalties, back taxes, and possible criminal charges.
laws.exceptions: Federal income taxes apply to all residents regardless of state income tax.

quiz.q: Does Georgia have a state income tax?
quiz.explanation: Georgia: Georgia has a flat income tax of 5.49% (transitioning from graduated rates).

laws.title: Sales Tax Rate
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §Revenue Code — 4.0% statewide sales tax
laws.fullDescription: Georgia has a 4.0% statewide sales tax. Georgia's state rate is 4%, but local taxes average 3.7%, making combined rates among the highest regionally. Combined state and local rates average 7.7%.
laws.penalty: Tax evasion: civil penalties and criminal charges for substantial violations.
laws.exceptions: Exempt items typically include: Groceries exempt from state tax (but not local taxes)..

quiz.q: What is the statewide sales tax rate in Georgia?
quiz.explanation: Georgia's statewide sales tax is 4.0%.

laws.title: Estate / Inheritance Tax — No
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §Revenue Code — No state estate tax
laws.fullDescription: Georgia: Georgia has no state estate tax.
laws.penalty: N/A — federal estate tax applies to all US residents with large estates.
laws.exceptions: Federal estate tax applies to estates over $13 million (2024).

quiz.q: Does Georgia have a state estate or inheritance tax?
quiz.explanation: Georgia: Georgia has no state estate or inheritance tax.

laws.title: Smoke-Free Workplace Law
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §Health Code — Clean Air Act / Smoke-Free law
laws.fullDescription: Georgia prohibits smoking in enclosed workplaces, restaurants, and bars.
laws.penalty: Violation: $100–$500 per incident for individuals.
laws.exceptions: Some private clubs and outdoor areas may be exempt.

quiz.q: Is smoking banned in workplaces and restaurants in Georgia?
quiz.explanation: Georgia: Comprehensive smoke-free law covers most indoor workplaces.

laws.title: Motorcycle Helmet Law
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §Vehicle Code — Universal helmet law
laws.fullDescription: Georgia: All motorcycle riders must wear helmets.
laws.penalty: Helmet violation: $100 fine.
laws.exceptions: N/A

quiz.q: Who must wear a motorcycle helmet in Georgia?
quiz.explanation: Georgia: Universal helmet law.

laws.title: Seatbelt Law
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §Vehicle Code — Mandatory seatbelts
laws.fullDescription: Georgia requires all front-seat occupants to wear seatbelts. Children under 8 or under 60 lbs must be in child safety seats.
laws.penalty: $25 fine for violations; higher for child restraint violations.
laws.exceptions: Some commercial vehicles and emergency situations may have limited exemptions.

quiz.q: Is the seatbelt law a primary offense in Georgia?
options: Yes, police can stop for seatbelt alone
quiz.explanation: Georgia's seatbelt law is a primary enforcement offense.

laws.title: Speed Limits
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §Vehicle Code — Statutory speed limits
laws.fullDescription: Georgia: Residential: 25 mph; highways: 65 mph; interstates: 70 mph; school zones: 20 mph. Posted limits vary.
laws.penalty: Speeding fines start at $50 and increase with severity; reckless driving is a criminal charge.
laws.exceptions: Emergency vehicles are exempt when responding.

quiz.q: What is the interstate speed limit in Georgia?
quiz.explanation: Georgia's standard interstate speed limit is 70 mph.

laws.title: Texting While Driving
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §Vehicle Code — Texting while driving banned
laws.fullDescription: Georgia: Texting while driving is prohibited.
laws.penalty: First offense: $50; repeat: $100.
laws.exceptions: Emergency 911 calls are permitted while driving.

quiz.q: Is texting while driving banned in Georgia?
quiz.explanation: Georgia: Georgia bans all handheld use while driving under the 2018 Hands-Free Georgia Act.

laws.title: DUI Checkpoint Legality
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §Vehicle Code — Sobriety checkpoints permitted
laws.fullDescription: DUI sobriety checkpoints are legal in Georgia. DUI checkpoints legal with proper procedures.
laws.penalty: N/A — this defines when checkpoints are legal.
laws.exceptions: Checkpoints must follow established procedures to be constitutional.

quiz.q: Are DUI sobriety checkpoints legal in Georgia?
quiz.explanation: Georgia: DUI checkpoints are legal with proper procedures.

laws.title: Move Over Law
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §Vehicle Code — Slow or move over for emergency vehicles
laws.fullDescription: Georgia's Move Over Law requires drivers to change lanes or slow down when passing stopped emergency vehicles and tow trucks and highway maintenance vehicles with flashing lights on the roadway or shoulder.
laws.penalty: Violation: $250 fine; if injury or death results, criminal charges may apply.
laws.exceptions: Required only when safe to do so without creating greater hazard.

quiz.q: Does Georgia's Move Over Law cover tow trucks?
quiz.explanation: Georgia's Move Over Law covers tow trucks.

laws.title: Cell Phone Use While Driving
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §40-6-241.2 — Handheld device restrictions
laws.fullDescription: Beyond texting, Georgia restricts handheld phone use while driving.
laws.penalty: Fines range from $50 to $200.
laws.exceptions: Hands-free calls and navigation use are generally permitted.

quiz.q: Can drivers make calls on a handheld phone while driving in Georgia?
quiz.explanation: Georgia: Handheld phone restrictions apply while driving.

laws.title: Age of Majority
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §Civil Code — Age 18 is legal adulthood
laws.fullDescription: In Georgia, the age of majority is 18. At 18, residents gain the right to vote, enter contracts, and make their own legal decisions. Age-specific restrictions still apply.
laws.penalty: N/A — this defines civil rights.
laws.exceptions: Some rights have higher age thresholds: alcohol (21), cannabis where legal (21).

quiz.q: What is the age of majority in Georgia?
quiz.explanation: Georgia's age of majority is 18, consistent with most US states.

laws.title: Voting Rights & Restoration
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §Election Code — Voter eligibility and felon restoration
laws.fullDescription: Georgia: Felons lose voting rights during incarceration; restoration rules vary by state.
laws.penalty: Voting while ineligible (while incarcerated): criminal charge.
laws.exceptions: Mentally incapacitated persons adjudicated incompetent may lose voting rights.

quiz.q: When are voting rights restored to a felon in Georgia?
quiz.explanation: Georgia: Voting rights restored after completing sentence.

laws.title: Jury Duty Requirements
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §Court Rules — Jury service
laws.fullDescription: Georgia citizens who are US citizens, 18+, registered voters (or driver's license holders) may be called for jury duty. Jurors receive $50/day. Employers must allow employees to serve.
laws.penalty: Willfully ignoring a jury summons: contempt of court, fines up to $500.
laws.exceptions: Exemptions include active military, police, extreme hardship, and some medical conditions.

quiz.q: What is the daily pay for jurors in Georgia?
quiz.explanation: Georgia jurors receive $50 per day for service.

laws.title: Mandatory Reporting of Child Abuse
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §Child Welfare Act — Mandatory reporters
laws.fullDescription: Georgia: Designated professionals are mandatory reporters. Reports must be made to child protective services or law enforcement. Good-faith reporters are protected from liability.
laws.penalty: Failure to report known child abuse: misdemeanor.
laws.exceptions: Attorney-client privilege may apply in limited circumstances.

quiz.q: Who must report suspected child abuse in Georgia?
quiz.explanation: Georgia: Designated professionals must report suspected child abuse.

laws.title: Age of Consent
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §Criminal Code — Age of consent is 16
laws.fullDescription: Georgia's age of consent is 16. Sexual activity with persons under the age of consent is a criminal offense. Sex offenders must register with the state registry.
laws.penalty: Sexual abuse of a minor: Felony with sex offender registration..
laws.exceptions: Romeo and Juliet provision: Romeo and Juliet provision may apply for close-in-age couples..

quiz.q: What is the age of consent in Georgia?
quiz.explanation: Georgia's age of consent is 16.

laws.title: Emancipation of Minors
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §Family Code — Court-ordered emancipation
laws.fullDescription: Georgia allows minors aged 16+ to petition for emancipation, granting adult legal status. The court considers whether it's in the minor's best interests and whether the minor can support themselves.
laws.penalty: N/A — emancipation is a civil court process.
laws.exceptions: Emancipation does not override minimum age laws for alcohol, cannabis, or voting.

quiz.q: At what minimum age can a minor petition for emancipation in Georgia?
quiz.explanation: Georgia allows minors aged 16+ to petition for emancipation.

laws.title: Curfew Laws for Minors
laws.subtitle: Local codes — Local ordinances only
laws.fullDescription: Georgia: No statewide curfew; municipalities set their own rules.
laws.penalty: Curfew violation: minor taken into custody and released to parents; parents may face fines.
laws.exceptions: Minors with employment, parental supervision, or school activities are typically exempt.

quiz.q: Does Georgia have a statewide youth curfew?
quiz.explanation: Georgia: Curfews set locally.

laws.title: Corporal Punishment in Schools
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §Education Code — Corporal punishment prohibited
laws.fullDescription: Georgia: Georgia permits corporal punishment in public schools. Many districts use it — Georgia is one of the top states for school corporal punishment usage.
laws.penalty: Educators using prohibited corporal punishment face administrative discipline and potential criminal charges.
laws.exceptions: Physical restraint to prevent imminent harm is permitted.

quiz.q: Is corporal punishment allowed in Georgia public schools?
quiz.explanation: Georgia: Corporal punishment is legal and commonly used in many Georgia school districts.

laws.title: Homeschooling Regulations
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §Education Code — Homeschooling requirements
laws.fullDescription: Georgia: Families must notify the school district and cover required subjects.
laws.penalty: Failure to provide required education: mandatory enrollment in public school.
laws.exceptions: Some states have additional oversight or assessment requirements.

quiz.q: Does Georgia have strict homeschooling regulations?
quiz.explanation: Georgia has moderate-regulation homeschooling with moderate requirements with notification and required subjects.

laws.title: School Vaccination Requirements
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §Health Code — Required vaccinations for school entry
laws.fullDescription: Georgia requires students to be vaccinated against standard childhood diseases for school entry. Standard vaccinations required for school entry.
laws.penalty: Unvaccinated students without exemptions may be excluded from school.
laws.exceptions: Exemptions available: medical and religious exemptions.

quiz.q: Can Georgia parents claim a philosophical exemption from school vaccinations?
quiz.explanation: Georgia vaccination exemptions: medical and religious exemptions.

laws.title: Abortion Laws
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §31-9B-1 — 6-week ban (LIFE Act)
laws.fullDescription: Georgia: Georgia's LIFE Act (2019) bans abortion after cardiac activity is detectable (~6 weeks), with exceptions for rape, incest, life of the mother, and fatal fetal abnormalities. The law took effect in 2022 after Dobbs.
laws.penalty: Performing illegal abortion: up to 10 years.
laws.exceptions: Medical emergencies to save the life of the mother are typically exempt.

quiz.q: What is the gestational limit on abortion in Georgia?
quiz.explanation: Georgia: Georgia bans abortion after ~6 weeks cardiac activity with limited exceptions for rape, incest, and mother's health.

laws.title: Death Penalty — Authorized
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §17-10-30 — Death penalty status
laws.fullDescription: Georgia has the death penalty. Georgia authorizes the death penalty for murder with aggravating circumstances. Georgia carries out executions by lethal injection.
laws.penalty: Death penalty crimes: Capital murder.
laws.exceptions: Federal death penalty may apply to federal crimes regardless of state law.

quiz.q: Does Georgia have the death penalty?
quiz.explanation: Georgia: Georgia has the death penalty for capital murder.

laws.title: Medical Aid in Dying (MAID)
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §Criminal Code — Assisted suicide illegal
laws.fullDescription: Georgia: Medical aid in dying is not legal.
laws.penalty: Assisting a suicide is a felony.
laws.exceptions: Withdrawal of life support and palliative sedation are legal with patient consent everywhere.

quiz.q: Is medical aid in dying (assisted suicide) legal in Georgia?
quiz.explanation: Georgia: Medical aid in dying is not legal.

laws.title: Drug Penalties (Non-Cannabis)
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §Controlled Substances Act — Controlled Substances Act
laws.fullDescription: Georgia controlled substance penalties: Drug penalties follow state scheduling.
laws.penalty: Possession of hard drugs: misdemeanor to felony. Distribution/manufacture: felony up to 30 years.
laws.exceptions: Prescribed medications used as directed are exempt.

quiz.q: Is simple drug possession a felony in Georgia?
quiz.explanation: Georgia: Drug penalties vary by substance and amount.

laws.title: Asset Forfeiture Laws
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §Criminal Code — Civil asset forfeiture
laws.fullDescription: Georgia: Civil asset forfeiture permitted for drug crimes.
laws.penalty: N/A — forfeiture is an action against property.
laws.exceptions: Innocent owner defense available: property returned if owner proves no criminal connection.

quiz.q: Does Georgia require a criminal conviction before forfeiture?
quiz.explanation: Georgia: Civil forfeiture allowed without conviction.

laws.title: Expungement & Record Sealing
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §Criminal Code — Expungement availability
laws.fullDescription: Georgia: Record sealing or expungement available for eligible offenses.
laws.penalty: N/A — this is a post-conviction relief process.
laws.exceptions: Serious felonies, sex offenses, and violent crimes generally cannot be expunged.

quiz.q: Can first-time non-violent offenders expunge their records in Georgia?
quiz.explanation: Georgia: Limited expungement available.

laws.title: Solitary Confinement Restrictions
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §Corrections Code — Restricted housing policies
laws.fullDescription: Georgia: DOC policies limit solitary confinement use.
laws.penalty: N/A — this governs prison administration.
laws.exceptions: Extremely dangerous inmates may face longer restricted housing.

quiz.q: Has Georgia restricted the use of solitary confinement?
quiz.explanation: Georgia: Limited reforms on solitary confinement.

laws.title: Private Prison Use
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §Corrections Code — Private correctional facilities

quiz.q: Does Georgia have a statewide body camera law?

laws.title: Police Use-of-Force Policies
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §Criminal Code — Justified use of force
laws.fullDescription: Georgia law: deadly force justified only when necessary to prevent death or serious injury.
laws.penalty: Unjustified use of force: potential criminal charges and civil liability.
laws.exceptions: Force always subject to the reasonableness standard.

quiz.q: When may Georgia officers use deadly force?
options: When reasonably necessary to prevent death or serious injury
quiz.explanation: Georgia officers may use deadly force only when reasonably necessary to prevent death or serious injury.

laws.title: Hate Crime Laws
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §Criminal Code — Bias-motivated crime laws
laws.fullDescription: Georgia has hate crime laws providing sentencing enhancements.
laws.penalty: Hate crime enhancement or separate charge: sentencing enhancement.
laws.exceptions: Protected speech expressing bias without accompanying criminal conduct is constitutionally protected.

quiz.q: Does Georgia have hate crime laws?

laws.title: Domestic Violence Laws & Protections
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §Domestic Violence Act — Domestic Violence Act
laws.fullDescription: Georgia: Comprehensive domestic violence protections including protective orders.
laws.penalty: Violation of DV protective order: misdemeanor to felony..
laws.exceptions: Mutual protective orders may be issued in some circumstances.

quiz.q: Does Georgia have mandatory arrest policies for domestic violence?

laws.title: Stalking & Cyberstalking Laws
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §Criminal Code — Stalking prohibition
laws.fullDescription: Georgia prohibits stalking — repeated non-consensual contact causing substantial distress. Stalking prohibits repeated unwanted contact causing distress. Cyberstalking covered.
laws.penalty: First-degree stalking: felony. Second-degree: misdemeanor.
laws.exceptions: Lawful investigations by law enforcement are not considered stalking.

quiz.q: Is cyberstalking (electronic harassment) covered by Georgia's stalking law?
quiz.explanation: Georgia's stalking law covers cyberstalking through electronic means.

laws.title: Consumer Data Privacy Law
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §Privacy Act — Data breach notification law
laws.fullDescription: Georgia: Georgia only has data breach notification requirements under the Georgia Personal Identity Protection Act.
laws.penalty: Data breach notification: civil fines per violation.
laws.exceptions: Small businesses may have reduced obligations under some state laws.

quiz.q: Does Georgia have a comprehensive consumer data privacy law?
quiz.explanation: Georgia: Georgia only has breach notification rules, not a comprehensive privacy law.

laws.title: Social Media Age Verification

laws.title: Environmental Regulations
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §Environmental Code — Environmental protection
laws.fullDescription: Georgia: State environmental agency enforces air, water, and waste regulations.
laws.penalty: Environmental violations: civil fines up to $25000/day; criminal penalties for willful violations.
laws.exceptions: Some agricultural and industrial uses have specific permitting pathways.

quiz.q: Which agency enforces environmental laws in Georgia?

laws.title: Renewable Energy Standards

quiz.q: Does Georgia have a Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS)?

quiz.q: Does Georgia have a bottle deposit/redemption law?

laws.title: Animal Cruelty Laws
laws.subtitle: O.C.G.A. §Criminal Code — Animal cruelty prohibition
laws.fullDescription: Georgia prohibits cruelty to animals including torture, beating, neglect, and fighting. Animal cruelty is a felony; neglect is a misdemeanor.
laws.penalty: Intentional cruelty: felony (up to 5 years). Neglect: misdemeanor (up to 1 year).
laws.exceptions: Lawful hunting, fishing, pest control, and veterinary procedures are exempt.

quiz.q: What is the maximum penalty for intentional animal cruelty in Georgia?
quiz.explanation: Georgia: Intentional animal cruelty is punishable by felony (up to 5 years).

laws.fullDescription: Georgia: Dangerous exotic animals are generally prohibited as pets.

quiz.q: Are large exotic cats (lions, tigers) legal as pets in Georgia?
quiz.explanation: Georgia: Large exotic cats banned as pets.

quiz.q: Are consumer aerial fireworks legal in Georgia?

laws.title: Gambling Laws

quiz.q: Are commercial casinos legal in Georgia?
